question: Will more F-16Vs land before New Year, yes or no?

lines.text: The first two touched down at Chihhang Air Base in Taitung around noon on Friday.
lines.note: Focus Taiwan 2 Oct 12:13 and 12:39 Taipei time

lines.text: They are the first of sixty-six in an eight billion dollar sale approved in 2019.
lines.note: Reuters; Focus Taiwan: NT$247.2bn, about US$8bn

lines.text: Deliveries were first meant to start in 2023, Taiwan's news agency says.
Reuters says issues including software problems delayed the planes.
lines.note: Reuters 2 Oct; Focus Taiwan also cites a production line move and supply chain disruption

lines.text: They left the US in August, flying via Hawaii and Guam.
lines.note: Migflug: departed 17 Aug via Fort Worth, Hawaii and Guam; SBS: via Guam

lines.text: Focus Taiwan says they sat in Hawaii without explanation, as President Trump prepared to meet Xi Jinping.
lines.note: Focus Taiwan 2 Oct; SBS: in Hawaii since 21 Sep

lines.text: They are Taiwan's first brand new fighters since French Mirage jets arrived in 1997.
lines.note: SBS: first new fighter jets in 29 years; last were Mirage 2000s delivered 1997

lines.text: Reuters says their radar is built to better counter China's air force, including the stealthy J-20.
lines.note: Reuters: 'to better counter the Chinese air force, including its stealthy J-20 fighters'

lines.text: With one hundred and thirty-nine upgraded older F-16s, Taiwan's fleet will pass two hundred.
lines.note: Focus Taiwan: 139 upgraded F-16A/Bs; Reuters: fleet to more than 200

lines.text: Defence Minister Wellington Koo says more are coming this year.

scene.quote: Of course we won't only have delivered these two by year-end

lines.text: Beijing has repeatedly told Washington to stop arming Taiwan, Reuters notes.
Two down, sixty-four to go. Will more F-16Vs land before New Year, yes or no?

caption: Taiwan's first F-16V Block 70 fighters have landed at Chihhang Air Base in Taitung, the first 2 of 66 jets in an $8 billion US sale approved in 2019. Software problems delayed them by years. Will more F-16Vs land before New Year, yes or no?
notes_full: First reported: Reuters preview 2 Oct about 02:20 UTC; landing around noon Taipei time 2 Oct (04:00 UTC), Focus Taiwan 12:13 Taipei; DW, Taipei Times, Flightglobal, SBS follow
Koo verbatim: 'Of course we won't only have delivered these two by year-end' (Reuters)

Reuters: 'issues including software problems have delayed delivery'; 'to better counter the Chinese air force, including its stealthy J-20 fighters'; 'Beijing has repeatedly told Washington to stop arming Taiwan'; fleet 'to more than 200 jets'

Focus Taiwan: 66 jets, NT$247.2bn (about US$8bn), approved Aug 2019, delivery to start 2023 and finish 2026; delays from production line relocation and supply chain; 139 upgraded F-16A/Bs; sat in Hawaii without explanation as Trump prepared to meet Xi
SBS: first new fighters in 29 years since Mirage 2000 in 1997; in Hawaii since 21 Sep
Left out: Global Times commentator's line about destroying the jets on the ground (threat framing); any invasion or blockade speculation
